# Cleaning and techniques

```{r cleaning}
# Cleaning
(BirdLife <- BirdLife %>%
  filter(Order1 == "Passeriformes", !is.na(Habitat.Density))%>%
  mutate(
    Habitat.Density = case_when(
      Habitat.Density == 1 ~ "Dense",
      Habitat.Density == 2 ~ "Open",
      Habitat.Density == 3 ~ "Open"
    ),
    Habitat.Density = fct_relevel(Habitat.Density, "Dense", "Open")
  ))
```


---

class: middle, center

# Exploratory Statistics

```{r, echo = FALSE}
#Summary statistics
Summary_table <- BirdLife %>%
  group_by(Habitat.Density) %>%
  summarise(mean.Mass.Habitat = mean(Mass), mean.wing.length.habitat = mean(Wing.Length), sum.of.species = n_distinct(Species1))

kable(Summary_table, format = "html")

```

# Distrubution of Body Mass

```{r recode-species, echo = FALSE}
# In this chunk I'm doing a bunch of analysis that I don't want to present 
bird_long <- BirdLife %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Mass, Wing.Length),
    names_to = "Trait",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Value_plot = if_else(Trait == "Mass", log10(Value), Value)
  )
# in my slides. But I need the resulting data frame for a plot I want to present.
iris_modified <- iris %>%
  mutate(Species = fct_other(Species, keep = "setosa"))
```

```{r plot-iris, echo = FALSE}
ggplot(BirdLife, aes(x = Mass, fill = Habitat.Density)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 10) +
  scale_x_log10() +
 facet_wrap(~ Habitat.Density) + 
  labs(title = "Mass Distribution by Habitat Density (log scale)",
       x = "Mass (log10 g)",
       y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# theme options: https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggtheme.html
```

# Modelling

If you want to generate a table, make sure it is in the HTML format (instead of Markdown or other formats), e.g.,

```{r iris-table, echo = FALSE}
set.seed(1122)
BirdLife_split <- initial_split(BirdLife)

train_data <- training(BirdLife_split)
test_data <- testing(BirdLife_split)

  
BirdLife_rec <- recipe(
  Habitat.Density ~ Mass + Wing.Length, 
  data = train_data
  ) %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors())

BirdLife_mod <- logistic_reg() %>%
  set_engine("glm")

BirdLife_wflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(BirdLife_mod) %>%
  add_recipe(BirdLife_rec)

BirdLife_fit <- BirdLife_wflow %>%
  fit(data = train_data)


(BirLife_train_pred <- predict(BirdLife_fit, train_data, type = "prob") %>%
  bind_cols(train_data))

BirLife_train_pred %>%
  roc_curve(
    truth = Habitat.Density,
    .pred_Dense,
    event_level = "first"
  ) %>%
  autoplot()
```

# Math Expressions

You can write LaTeX math expressions inside a pair of dollar signs, e.g. &#36;\alpha+\beta$ renders $\alpha+\beta$. You can use the display style with double dollar signs:

```
$$\bar{X}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^nX_i$$
```

$$\bar{X}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^nX_i$$

Limitations:

1. The source code of a LaTeX math expression must be in one line, unless it is inside a pair of double dollar signs, in which case the starting `$$` must appear in the very beginning of a line, followed immediately by a non-space character, and the ending `$$` must be at the end of a line, led by a non-space character;

1. There should not be spaces after the opening `$` or before the closing `$`.

1. Math does not work on the title slide (see [#61](https://github.com/yihui/xaringan/issues/61) for a workaround).
